sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Union County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Union County splits the work between the PVA, the sheriff and the county clerk, and the PVA and the sheriff both list 100 West Main Street in Morganfield. The PVA appraises property as of January 1 each year. The county's PVA page is explicit that the office does not set tax rates, calculate taxes or collect them.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437, phone (270) 389-1933, open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Exemption applications go here.
  • Sheriff, who collects the bill: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437, phone (270) 389-1303, open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00.
  • County Clerk, who holds deeds and any delinquent bill after April 15: (270) 389-1334.

The county government site also hosts a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA menu, which help you check a parcel before you talk to anyone.

sections.h2: What makes Union County a different housing market from its neighbors?
sections.html:
Union County sits in the northwest corner of Kentucky, on the east bank of the Ohio River opposite the mouth of the Wabash. Illinois and Indiana both touch it, and the county forms part of the tri-state point with Posey County, Indiana and Gallatin County, Illinois. It lies in the Western Coal Fields region, with low wooded hills and level farmland, and four cities: Morganfield (the seat), Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly.

US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 are the main roads. The John T. Myers Locks and Dam on the Ohio, finished in 1977, sits about three and a half miles below Uniontown. Public schools run through Union County Public Schools, with elementary schools in Morganfield, Sturgis and Uniontown, one middle school and Union County High School, plus a private Catholic school in Morganfield.

The numbers contrast with Warren County. Union is shrinking while Warren grows, and homes cost far less.

With no new building permits recorded for 2025 and a median value near $100,000, nearly every sale here is a resale of an older house, so the condition of the house and the state of the tax account matter to any offer.

sections.h2: What does the state's tax rate mean for a Union County house?
sections.html:
The state's real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, lowered from 10.9 cents the year before because assessments rose faster than the 4 percent limit. On a house at Union County's $104,500 median value, the state share is $110.77. County, school, library and other districts add their own rates, so the full bill is higher.

Owners aged 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program, can take a $49,100 homestead exemption for 2025 and 2026. At the median value, the taxable base drops to $55,400 and the state share to about $58.72. In Union County 21.9 percent of residents are 65 or over, and 23.1 percent of those under 65 report a disability, so the exemption is relevant to many owners.

Apply at the PVA on West Main Street. Disability claims renew every year, except for veterans with a service connected disability and owners found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What are the Union County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Kentucky law, KRS 134.015, sets a single calendar for the sheriff. Paying in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount. From November 2 to December 31 the face amount is due, in January a 5 percent penalty applies, and from February the penalty is 10 percent, with the sheriff adding a further fee on top.

The sheriff holds delinquent listings until April 15. On that date every unpaid bill goes to the County Clerk, and a lien is recorded on the property. The clerk's page says the county sale of those delinquent bills is typically held in September of the year after taxes are due, with the date posted on the county website about a month ahead.

Buyers at the sale must register with the clerk. Anyone planning to buy more than three certificates in the county, more than five statewide, or to invest more than $10,000 must also register with the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: How much more does a delinquent Union County bill cost?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue publishes worked examples on a $1,000 bill. When it passes from sheriff to clerk it stands at $1,254.00 after the 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and an assumed 4 percent commission. From there the climb is steady.

  • After the county attorney's first notice: $1,611.30.
  • Paid in May: $1,627.61, since a second month of interest raises the commissions.
  • Paid in June after advertising: $1,659.90.
  • Bought by a third party at the sale: $1,704.21, before that buyer adds its own interest and fees.

Interest runs at 1 percent a month from the transfer. The lien survives up to 11 years under KRS 134.420 and goes with the land, so a Union County owner who plans to sell should clear the account or arrange for the title company to pay it from proceeds.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Union County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA first, because Kentucky does not accept an appeal from an owner who skipped the conference. The real property roll is open to the public for 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the PVA publishes the schedule in the county's largest newspaper.

After the conference, you file with the County Clerk by the close of business on the day after the inspection period ends. The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days later for up to five days. Bring sale comparisons, repair estimates and photographs, since a board must deny an appeal that arrives without factual evidence. If you skip the board or miss the hearing, you lose the right to carry the case on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

The board explains any change in writing, and you may record the hearing. A higher final value produces a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What does a Union County deed need, and where is it recorded?
sections.html:
The County Clerk records deeds, mortgages, assignments and mortgage releases at 100 West Main Street, and the books go back to 1811. Kentucky requires a deed to be recorded in the county where the land lies, and the new deed must cite where the seller got title. Under KRS 382.135 it must also name both parties with mailing addresses, state the full consideration, give an in care of address for the year's tax bill and carry a sworn certificate of value signed by both sides.

The clerk's office offers e-filing so that a title company can send documents without mailing them. Union County residents can search records at no charge from home, limited to five searches a day, and everyone can use the terminals in the office. For commercial users the monthly rate through the county's records vendor is $65 per county.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Union County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Union County Sheriff at 100 West Main Street in Morganfield, phone (270) 389-1303. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, and the mailing address is PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437.

faqs.q: Does the Union County PVA set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The PVA only appraises property as of January 1 and processes exemptions. Rates come from the taxing districts, and the sheriff sends and collects the bill.

faqs.q: When is the Union County delinquent tax sale held?
faqs.a: It is typically held in September of the year after the taxes were due. The County Clerk posts the date on the county website about a month beforehand, and the clerk's phone is (270) 389-1334.

faqs.q: Can I check a Union County parcel online before I list it?
faqs.a: Yes. The county government site carries a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages. Use them to confirm the owner of record and the assessed value.

faqs.q: How long does an unpaid Union County tax lien last?
faqs.a: It lasts until the debt is paid or 11 years pass, under KRS 134.420. It stays with the property when ownership changes, so a buyer's title company will ask for it to be cleared.
